title: Tableau circuit decides the language
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the binary alphabet whose head positions at each time depend only on input length. Let $L$ be a language of binary words and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every binary word $y$, the machine halts within the specified time $T(|y|)$ and outputs the one-bit indicator of whether $y\in L$. Then for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every binary input $x$ of length $n$, the tableau circuit for $M$ with parameters $n,T(n)$ outputs the indicator of whether $x\in L$.
